cards.question: What is the definition of variable lifetime (storage duration) in C?
cards.answer: The period during program execution in which memory is guaranteed to be reserved and valid for an object.

cards.question: What are the three primary categories of storage duration (lifetime) in C?
cards.answer: Automatic (stack lifetime bound to block scope), static (entire program lifetime in data/BSS segment), and allocated (dynamic heap lifetime managed via malloc/free).

cards.question: How does a variable lifetime differ when declared as auto int x versus static int x inside a function?
cards.answer: auto int x is created on the stack when the block is entered and destroyed on exit, whereas static int x is created before main() starts and persists until program termination.
